description: Before proposing a PostgreSQL migration, MEASURE what each statement would lock, instead of guessing. Runs your schema (DDL + sample data) and then the migration in an ephemeral PostgreSQL (pglite, in memory) and reads, per statement: the strongest table lock actually taken (pg_locks), whether it rewrote the table, whether it scanned it in full, a risk level (lock mode × duration), and the safer rewrite when there is one — CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, ADD CONSTRAINT … NOT VALID + VALIDATE, NOT NULL NOT VALID (PG 18), lock_timeout, new column + backfill instead of ALTER TYPE — with the SQL written out. Nothing touches a real database.

migration.description: The migration to measure, one or more statements

queries.description: Optional: the application's queries. Each one is run before and after the migration and reported as breaks / changes (columns removed or retyped) / widens / fixes / already-failing / same

schema.description: The starting schema: CREATE TABLE … plus a few INSERTs so scans and rewrites are visible. Can be empty

name: db_migration_measure
